hook.text: He spent three hours on his best subject and thirty minutes on his worst. His worst subject sank his grade.

buildup.text: Learners gravitate toward topics that feel comfortable. Comfort means mastery; discomfort signals the real need.

discovery.text: Metacognitive planners allocate more time to weak areas. This feels harder but yields the highest marginal gain.

twist.text: Studying your strongest subject is a form of procrastination. It feels productive but avoids the real challenge.

climax.text: Rank subjects by difficulty. Spend twice as much time on the hardest one. Revisit strong areas briefly.

punchline.text: Spend time where you're weakest. That is strategic.

quiz.question: Why do learners tend to over-study strong subjects?
options: Strong subjects have more material to cover
Comfort feels productive while discomfort is avoided
Teachers assign more homework in strong subjects
